environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: After poisoning, a GET victim is served from cache at zero fetches. A HEAD to the same target also hits with zero fetches and returns 200 with the poisoned Content-Length: 50 header and no body; a Range: bytes=0-1 GET hits with zero fetches and returns the full 50-byte poisoned body at 200 (no 206, no slicing); a fabricated If-None-Match also hits at zero fetches and serves the full 200 poison because the stored upstream headers carry no ETag for the local 304 path to compare. Only a POST refetches (hit 5), so method is not part of the key and HEAD widens the poison to HEAD consumers.
findings.title: HEAD and Range are served from the poisoned entry; 304 is unreachable; POST bypasses

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line
